topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and introduces its learning objectives.

topics.label: Genetic origins and cellular evolution of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations accumulate and enable cancer development according to cellular context and inherited susceptibility.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks, chance and population variation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk despite uncertainty and variation between individuals and populations.

topics.label: Infectious causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive carcinogenesis, with Burkitt lymphoma illustrating the interaction between pathogens and their host environment.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce DNA damage through mechanisms shaped by their chemical properties and metabolism.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how tumour promoters enable the growth of mutation-bearing cells rather than acting solely through direct mutagenesis.

topics.label: Tissue and developmental susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain context-dependent susceptibility to carcinogens and consolidate it within the preceding account of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Methods and limitations of establishing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence can identify carcinogenic exposures and assess their effects while accounting for the limitations of each investigative approach.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and framing everyday exposure decisions as risk–benefit judgments.
